newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian court delays Rao trial in vote-buying case.
newsitem.headline: Indian court delays Rao trial in vote-buying case.

text.p: An Indian court has postponed the trial of former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao in a vote-buying case until August 8, Rao's counsel said on Tuesday.
A special court of inquiry last week indicted Rao and 19 others on charges of criminal conspiracy and abetting bribery. The trial date had been set for May 14.

Lawmakers of regional Jharkand Mukti Morcha (JMM) party have alleged that they were paid $100,000 to vote against a 1993 no-confidence motion that Rao's Congress-led government survived by a narrow margin.
"The Delhi High Court has stayed the proceedings in the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha case until 8th August," Rao's counsel R.K. Anand told Reuters.
The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) last year filed a case accusing Rao and other Congress leaders of buying the votes. They have denied any wrongdoing.
The CBI also indicted Rao in the case and charged him with conspiracy to pay JMM legislators $100,000 to vote against the no-confidence motion.
The charges of bribery and conspiracy carry a maximum penalty of five years in prison.
Rao had filed two applications in the court to quash charges made by the CBI. The Delhi Court directed CBI to reply to Rao's petitions by August 8.
Rao, who led his Congress party to its worst-ever defeat in general elections last year, has been named in two other criminal cases relating to forgery and cheating.
He has denied any wrongdoing in all of the cases and has obtained preventive bail in all three.
Rao quit as Congress chief last September after a judge ordered him to appear in court in the criminal cheating case.
